newsitem.title: UK: Sterling Eurobond spreads unmoved by rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Sterling Eurobond spreads unmoved by rate rise.

text.p: Spreads on sterling Eurobonds were unchanged on Thursday after British interest rates went up to 6.75 percent from 6.50 percent, traders said.
"The rate rise will not cause much movement at all (in spreads)," a Eurosterling trader said.
The market had factored in a rate increase of up to half a percentage point as Britain tries to cool consumer demand and meet its inflation target. A further rate rise is anticipated.
"People are now expecting another increase, which might put investors off buying at current levels," a Eurobond syndicate manager at a British bank said.
The benchmark short-dated Eurosterling bond, a Fannie Mae 6.875 percent June 2002 deal, was trading at around 14 basis points over gilts, bankers said.
"Spreads will remain steady for now," another Eurosterling trader said.

"But we will keep an eye on the currency. If rates are seen to have peaked, which is not the case yet, the currency might come off a bit and lead to selling, which in turn might widen spreads," he said.
The pound lost over a pfennig to close to 2.95 marks but quickly regained ground. Traders said it would remain favoured, with demand boosted by the allure of further rate rises.
At 1300 GMT the pound was trading at 2.9555/65 marks.
